【音乐】嗨,大家,我是Fiona。在前几个课程中,我们谈论了很多关于电子效应的事情。今天,我们将继续谈论电子效应。在今天的课程中,你们将学习词词和词词的相对性和相对性。在课程结束后,我希望你们可以使用相对性和相对性在现实情况中。请准备你的学生书和工作室。首先,让我们来看看一些电子效应的课程。请回答这些问题。第一,电子效应有多大?电子效应比车大。第二,电子效应有多大?我们可能比我们意识到的电子效应要大。第三,课程中的写者说,电子效应比一个人更聪明?当中,答案是不的。第四,为什么一个人比电子效应更聪明?因为,一个人的脑子能理解东西的意义更好,并创造新的想法。现在,读一下词词,并找到相对性和相对性的词词。在1940年代,电子效应比车大。Bigger is the comparative form of the adjective big.Your brain can understand the meaning of things better.Better is the comparative form of the adverb well.This is the most expensive computer I have ever bought.The most expensive is the superlative form of the adjective expensive.The desktop works the most quickly of the three computers.The most quickly is the superlative form of the adverb quickly.In today's lesson, we'll talk about the comparatives and superlatives of adjectives and adverbs.How can we form the comparative and superlative of adjectives and adverbs?Do you know the rules?You may look at the table and discover the rules for the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives and adverbs.As you can see, we add ER and EST to one syllable adjectives and adverbs.一般在单音节形容词或复词词位加 ER或 EST,like small, smaller, smallest.If a one-syllable adjective or adverb ending with a silent letter E, we only add R and ST.在以不翻译的字母E结尾的词词位加R或ST,like wide, wider, widest.If a one-syllable adjective or adverb ending with a single vowel plus a single consonant,we double the final consonant before adding ER and EST.以中读B音节结尾且末尾只有一个符音字母的形容词或复词构成比较级或最高级时,要双写这个符音字母再加ER或EST,like big, bigger, biggest.For two-syllable adjectives or adverbs ending with a consonant plus Y,we change the Y to I and add ER and EST.以符音字母加Y结尾的双音节词构成比较级或最高级时,要先把Y改为I,再加ER或EST,like happy, happier, happiest.For some two-syllable adjectives or adverbs,we can either add ER and EST,or use more plus the word to form the comparative,and use most plus the word to form the superlative.一些双音节的形容词或者复词构成比较级或最高级时,我们既可以在词尾直接加ER或EST,也可以用more或most加原籍的形式,like clever, cleverer, cleverest,or clever, more clever, most clever.We use more and most for adverbs that end with ly,以ly结尾的复词构成比较级或最高级时,直接加more或者most,like slowly, more slowly, most slowly.For words of three syllables or more,we use more plus the adjective or the adverb to form the comparative,and the most to form the superlative.多音节词要在前面加more构成比较级,加most构成最高级,like expensive, more expensive, most expensive.Some adjectives and adverbs have irregular comparative and superlative forms.Think about the irregular forms of the comparatives and superlatives of these words listed in the table.Let's read together.Good, well, better, best.Bad, badly, worse, worst.Many, much, more, most.Little, less, least.Far, farther, farthest.Far, further, furthest.We usually use farther and farthest to talk about distance.When we talk about the degree or extent of something,we use further and furthest.Further can also mean more or additional.Now, have you got a clear picture about the rules for the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives and adverbs in your mind?Please have a try to check your understanding.Now, take out your worksheet and fill in the table.Let's check the answers.Soft is a one syllable adjective.So we just add er and est to the end of the word.Soft softer softest.Large is a one syllable adjective.Large is a one-syllable adjective, which ends with a silent letter E, so we just add R and S-T, large, larger, largest.Heavy is a two-syllable adjective, ending with a consonant plus Y, so we change the Y to I and add E-R and E-S-T, heavy, heavier, heaviest.Thin is a one-syllable adjective, ending with a single vowel plus a single consonant, so we double the final consonant N and then add E-R and E-S-T, thin, thinner, thinnest.Simple has two ways to change its form into comparative and superlative, so we can say simple, simpler, simplest, or simple, more simple, most simple.Quietly is an adverb ending with L-Y, so we put more and most before the word.Quietly, more quietly, most quietly.Comfortable is a multi-syllable adjective, so we put more and most before it.Comfortable, more comfortable, most comfortable.Now, read the sentences again and discover the rules of using comparatives.When we compare two things or two groups of things, we use the comparative form of adjectives or adverbs.In the first sentence, the first computers and cars are compared, and the first computers were bigger.After comparatives, we can use then to link two parts of a comparison.So we can rewrite the second sentence in this way.Your brain can understand the meaning of things better than a computer.Let's practice.Complete the sentences using the comparative forms of the words in the box.Use then where necessary.Check the answersNumber oneI felt tired last nightSo I went to bed earlier than usualNumber twoUnfortunatelyThe problem was more difficult than we thought at firstNumber threeYou look thinnerHave you lost weightNumber fourI'm sorry.I didn't catch youCan you speak more slowly pleaseNumber fiveIn some parts of the countryPrices are higher than in othersNumber sixYour English has improvedIt's better than beforeLet's read the sentencesAnd discover the rules of using superlativesWhen do we use superlativesWhen we compare more than two thingsOr two groups of thingsWe use the superlative form of adjectives or adverbsFrom the first sentenceWe can know thatI have bought more than two computersAnd the laptop is the most expensive oneWe usually use definite articleBefore the superlative form of adjectivesBefore the superlative form of adverbsDefinite article the can be omittedLet's have a tryComplete the sentencesUsing the superlative forms of the words in the boxPokéDex Speaking of champions listening to cliche drawsLet's check the answersNumber oneI didn't take much moneySo we stayed at the cheapest hotel in the townNumber 2it was an awful dayIt was the worst day of my life.Number 3.What is the most popular sport in your country?I like Sunday.For me, it's the most enjoyable day of the week.Tom is good at sports.He jumps the farthest in our class.Which is the shortest way to the supermarket?This is a more challenging task for you to check if you can use comparatives and superlatives well.Complete the sentences with the comparative or superlative forms of the words in the brackets.但我感觉今天不是太累,所以我只是在做一个对手炫耀的最后一项工作。或者是喜欢做人的工作吧。今天我做了两项工作。整个工作,从人生到速度,我觉得是最好的。第一项是的确实历史,所以一旦有机会就能完成我做的工作。I wasn't feeling well yesterday, but I feel a bit better today.What's the most expensive thing you've ever bought?I prefer this chair to the other one.It's more comfortable.Who is the fastest runner?I can remember when I was three years old.It's the earliest memory.The building is the tallest one in our city.It is taller than any other building.This knife isn't very sharp.Do you have a sharper one?No, it's the sharpest one I have.It's time for you to use comparatives and superlatives in the conversation.Your friend David needs a new computer, but he has no idea whether to choose a desktop, a laptop, or a tablet.Complete the conversation with comparatives or superlatives.Let's look at how my student John completes the conversation.I will read the dialogue for you.I need a new computer.I'm not sure whether to buy a desktop, a laptop, or a tablet.What do you need it for?I want to have a new one for online learning.You need a big screen.Desktops usually have the biggest screens.I also need it for my homework.I need to type a lot on it.I type more quickly on the keyboard than on the tablet.Oh, but sometimes I need to take it to school.Come on, it's meaningless to consider desktops.Tablets are much lighter than laptops.And I want to store as many things as possible.You can store more things on the laptop than on the tablet.Thanks for your suggestion.I will buy a laptop.John uses comparatives and superlatives to talk about the advantages of different kinds of computers.Good job!Do you still remember the names of the equipment?CD-ROMs, DVD-ROMs, flash disks, and mobile hard disks are all storage equipment.Suppose your grandmother wants to know the differences between them.Can you talk about them?Try to use the comparative and superlative forms of the adjectives and adverbs in the box.I want to buy a laptop.I want to buy a tablet.I want to store as many things as possible.I want to open a bank account.staring out his eyes, whoever we may be.Let's take a look at how my student Roger talks about the storage equipment.Mobile hard disks are the biggest.We can store more things on mobile hard disks than on DVD rooms or on flash disks.Flash disks are the smallest and the lightest so they can be carried most easily.Usually mobile hard disks are the most expensive and DVD rooms are the cheapest.Roger uses the comparatives and superlatives correctly.Well done!When you try to introduce something new to others, you can try to use comparatives and superlatives to make your explanation clearer.I hope you can use comparatives and superlatives in your real-life situations.Here is your homework.Thank you for watching.
